angle: Stop scrubbing grout on your knees with a tiny brush; stand up and clean the lines faster with the proper grout brush and formula.
hook: If you're still cleaning grout like this, your knees are doing all the work.

angle: A regular mop can wipe tile surfaces but leave the grout lines looking dark; use the stand-up V-shaped grout brush and professional-strength formula to target the lines instead of just spreading water across the floor.
hook: Your mop is cleaning the tile, but it is skipping the grout lines.

angle: General spray-and-wipe cleaning makes grout look wet for a second but leaves the dark lines behind; target the grout directly with the V-shaped brush and professional-strength formula.
hook: If your grout only looks clean while it’s wet, this is the problem.

angle: A flat sponge keeps sliding over recessed grout and wasting effort; the V-shaped stand-up brush drops into the line so the professional-strength formula can work where the grime actually sits.
hook: That flat sponge is riding right over the dirty grout.

angle: An old toothbrush forces tiny back-and-forth strokes that leave grout cleaning slow and uncomfortable; switch to a V-shaped stand-up grout brush with professional-strength cleaner to cover grout lines more directly.
hook: That old toothbrush is turning one grout line into a whole project.

angle: A flat, wide push broom just bends across the tile surface and completely ignores the deep grout lines; switch to the V-shaped brush and professional formula that specifically target the narrow recessed grime.
hook: Your standard floor broom is just bending over the dirt in your grout lines.
